correctness.rationale: A thin SVD reduces the iteration to positive scalar multipliers g_alpha(t) with residual update h_alpha(t)=1-(1-t)g_alpha(t)^2. Differentiation and evaluation at t_* give the stated maximum, whose difference from 1+1/(2alpha) is the positive prefactor times the cubic. The maximum is strictly increasing (compare at a positive maximizer, or from its boundary value 1 at alpha=3/8), whereas the comparison function decreases. Below the crossing, t in (0,1) maps into (-1/(2u),t). On (-1/(2u),0), the second-order Taylor polynomial upper bounds (1-t)^(-1/2), since the third derivative is positive and t is negative; hence 0<g_alpha(t)<1 and t<h_alpha(t)<=0. Uniform strict drift at any nonzero candidate limit then gives scalar convergence for every schedule, and the multipliers preserve the polar branch. The exact polynomial h_alpha(t)/t^2 extends jointly continuously at zero on the full compact interval [-1/(2u),1] times [3/8,u], so the claimed uniform inequality even holds with K=0 after enlarging C_u; this says nothing about a condition-number-independent entrance time into a small residual neighborhood. At the maximizing start the endpoint lands on the nonunit g=1 fixed point; above it the same start crosses the fixed point and the scalar increases without a finite limit. Independent rational spot checks of the identities and bisection corroborated the root 1.472229260972032370849477394..., but the universal result is analytic.
